Prasugrel.Recommendation: Recommended in P2Y12 receptor inhibitor–naive patients proceeding to PCI
Prasugrel.Dose: 60 mg LD, 10 mg o.d. MD; 5 mg o.d. MD for patients ≥75 years or weight <60 kg

Ticagrelor.Recommendation: Recommended irrespective of treatment strategy (invasive or conservative)
Ticagrelor.Dose: 180 mg LD, 90 mg twice a day MD

Clopidogrel.Recommendation: Recommended when prasugrel or ticagrelor are not available, not tolerated, or contraindicated

DAPT and CABG.Recommendation: If patients presenting with ACS stop DAPT to undergo CABG, resume DAPT after surgery for at least 12 months

Glycoprotein IIb/IIIa antagonists.Recommendation: Pre-treatment with a glycoprotein IIb/IIIa antagonist is not recommended

P2Y12 receptor pre-treatment in NSTE-ACS.Recommendation: Routine pre-treatment with a P2Y12 receptor inhibitor in NSTE-ACS patients in whom coronary anatomy is not known and early invasive management (<24 h) is planned is not recommended

General.Recommendation: Parenteral anticoagulation is recommended for all patients with ACS at time of diagnosis

UFH bolus during PCI.Recommendation: Routine use of a UFH bolus (weight-adjusted i.v. bolus during PCI of 70–100 IU/kg) is recommended in patients undergoing PCI

Fondaparinux.Recommendation: Fondaparinux is not recommended in patients with STEMI undergoing PPCI
For patients with NSTE-ACS in whom early invasive angiography (within 24 h) is not anticipated, fondaparinux is recommended

Atrial fibrillation strategy.Recommendation: Default strategy for patients with atrial fibrillation and CHA2DS2-VASc score ≥1 in men and ≥2 in women: after up to 1 week of triple antithrombotic therapy following the ACS event, dual antithrombotic therapy using a non–vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulant at the recommended dose
